citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
A tamarin was found collapsed and recumbent on the bottom of its outdoor enclosure and the veterinarian was contacted
to assist. The tamarin was treated on site, but according to the attending veterinarian, an appropriate treatment could not
be fully administered due to the unavailability of a glucometer and necessary dextrose. Additionally, per the case
summary notes provided by the attending veterinarian, the lack of cooling devices also impeded the treatment process.
Despite all efforts the tamarin subsequently expired.
Due to the lack of the appropriate equipment, animal treatment could not be fully and successfully completed. This is
considered inadequate veterinary care. Each dealer or exhibitor shall establish and maintain programs of adequate
veterinary care that include: The availability of appropriate facilities, personnel, equipment, and services to comply with
the provisions of this subchapter.
TO BE CORRECTED BY: OCTOBER 17, 2026

The following items are in need of repair and/or replacement.
DEER SHELTER E-1
• Upon entering the shelter building, the front right post of the white-tailed deer shelter is severely rotted at its base. The
wood is deteriorated in such a way that the post is no longer attached to the ground.
• The front exterior wall, on the left, is detached from the framework thus leaving exposed nails visible.
• The front exterior wall, on the left, is deteriorated along the entire base with a gap present due to missing and damaged
wood.
• On the interior wall on the left, there is a gap at the base that measures approximately 6 inches by 4 inches that leaves
the wall no longer flush with the ground.
LLAMA/ALPCA SHELTER
• The edges of the roof, on both sides, are missing sections of wood, thus leaving the roof edges in disrepair.
The above listed damaged wooden shelters, walls, posts, and roof edges shall be repaired to protect the deer, alpacas,
and llama from injury and to ensure the structural strength of the structures.
The facility must be constructed of such material and of such strength as appropriate for the animals involved. The interior
and outdoor housing facilities shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to protect the animals
from injury and to contain the animals.
TO BE CORRECTED BY: OCTOBER 17, 2026
This inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:

APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
